name: contract-negotiation
description: Negotiate a contract once and observe the outcome, then prove a second negotiation on the same offer is refused (one attempt per offer, #1366), then accept and attempt delivery. The file's original version never called `contract negotiate` at all; rewritten to exercise the actual negotiation mechanic (issue #479 follow-up).

steps.description: Negotiation attempt on the supply/dirtite offer (the only attempt it gets, #1366). The target is fixed at the supply/dirtite offer throughout this file rather than read back from `contract list`'s text output, which expect can't do.

expect.note: negotiating costs nothing and moves no count -- the only real effect is on the contract's own terms, which no state field exposes. The outcome (success or failure) depends on the per-attempt RNG stream and is not pinned here.

steps.description: A tick passes between the first attempt and the refused retry, so the refusal below cannot be explained by an identical same-tick roll.
Second negotiation on the same offer is refused (one attempt per offer, #1366): the console answers `already negotiated`, and the card's negotiate button is disabled in the panel.

expect.note: the refused retry leaves the contract's terms and cash untouched; the negotiate button on that card is disabled with the 'Already negotiated' tooltip.

steps.description: #513/#581/#635: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-type="supply"][data-contract-material="dirtite"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted the supply/dirtite contract literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-type`/`data-contract-material` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it -- and, unlike the numeric id it replaces (#635), survives the offer pool rotating past it.

role: guard (issue #515): both the amount input and DELIVER button are genuinely disabled here — `amountInput.disabled = maxDeliverable <= 0` and `deliverBtn.disabled = maxDeliverable <= 0` (ContractsPanel.ts) — this file's scope is negotiation and accept/decline, not the full haul-to-storage pipeline, so nothing is ever in storage. A real click cannot land on either control, so this proves the same refusal `expect.blocked` already asserted (now scoped to `[data-contract-type="supply"][data-contract-material="dirtite"]`, issue #513/#635) rather than performing one.

expect.note: the contract stays active/undelivered -- this file's scope is negotiation and accept/decline, not the full haul-to-storage pipeline
